title: Self-Awareness
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 3 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Gender is taught as Genesis 1:27 states it, kindly, without comparing boys and girls; a child who is sad or upset at home is listened to privately (FAITH: teacher of the school's tradition to confirm wording).

skills.key_step: The child says God created people male and female in his image (Genesis 1:27), and both are equally loved.

floor.question: Who created the sun and the moon?

representations: pictures of boys and girls doing many activities
steps: Say "God made me a boy" or "a girl".
Say both are in God's image.
contexts: a class of boys and girls
a family with sons and daughters

board.do: Write Genesis 1:27: male and female he created them.
Wait for the child to say God.
Write: God made me, God loves me.

misconceptions.ask: Whom did God create in his image, according to Genesis 1:27?
misconceptions.repair: Read Genesis 1:27 slowly: male and female he created them. Both in God's image.

misconceptions.ask: Who created people male and female?
misconceptions.repair: Link Genesis 1:27 and Psalm 139:13: God forms each child.

misconceptions.ask: Wanjiru plays football. Is she still a girl?
misconceptions.repair: List activities both boys and girls do. Being a boy or girl is how God made you, not what you play.

misconceptions.ask: What does "made in God's image" teach us?
misconceptions.repair: Talk about a child "taking after" a parent in kindness, not only looks.

checks.question: According to Genesis 1:27, who created male and female?
Does God love boys more than girls?

skills.key_step: The child describes good ways of coping with happy and sad feelings: pray, share, talk to a trusted adult, calm down.

floor.prerequisite: Knows himself or herself as God's creation.
floor.question: Who made you?

steps: Name the feeling in the story.
Say a good way to cope.
Say a way that does not help.

board.do: Write two columns: helps, does not help.
Point at the card "hit your friend".
board.say: Does this help when you are angry?

board.do: Wait for the child to say no and give a better way.

listen_for: Keep it inside and tell nobody
misconceptions.ask: You feel very sad. What can you do?
misconceptions.repair: Role-play telling a trusted adult. Say: sharing a sad feeling helps.

misconceptions.ask: A friend takes your pencil and you feel angry. What should you do?
misconceptions.repair: Practise calm steps: breathe, count, speak, get help.

misconceptions.ask: You got the best marks. What is a good way to show you are happy?
misconceptions.repair: Contrast two pictures: a child laughing at others and a child thanking God and helping.

misconceptions.ask: Can a child pray to God when sad about a small thing?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Peter 5:7 (cast all your anxiety on him) in simple words.

checks.question: Name a good way to cope when sad.
checks.answer: Pray (talk to a parent or teacher)

checks.question: Is hitting a good way to deal with anger?
